title: Distractors from the words taught
statement: In a word-meaning check, make every wrong option a word the lesson taught, because an untaught word can be ruled out by unfamiliarity alone and so tests nothing.
detail: The reading course's content-failure log adds this to its vocabulary gate: a meaning-check distractor must be a word the lesson teaches, since a distractor naming an untaught word can only be eliminated by unfamiliarity (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-3/CONTENT-FAILURE-CLASSES.md`, lines 73-74). It is one rule from one log, with no count of how many checks broke it.

evidence.quote: Also: a meaning-check distractor must be a word **this lesson teaches**.
A distractor naming an untaught word can only be eliminated by unfamiliarity, so it tests nothing.
Fix: distractors in the same form (enchanting → boring, puzzling, soothing; menacing → comforting, welcoming, charming).
